name: Sylara
description: The Adventurers' Guild master â€” close-cropped silver hair, Guild insignia, and eyes that read System profiles the way other people read faces.
flavor_text: She's been Guild Master since before the Fracture. She remembers what adventuring was like when the System wasn't watching.

root.npc_text: Sylara looks up from a stack of reports and glances at your System profile with that slight unfocusing of the eyes. 'What do you need?'
root.smart_observation: She's been reviewing incident reports, not contract forms. Something's happened that isn't public yet.
root.perception_reveal: Her composure is professional but not easy. There's a careful weight behind her words â€” the kind you get from carrying information you can't share.

options.label: Tell me about the dungeon.
options.npc_response: 'Standard briefing: Floor 1 is Rank F â€” goblins, slimes, the occasional large spider. Good for new classifications. Stay on the first floor until your rank improves. Don't ignore your System compass.'

options.label: What happened to the survey teams on Floor 2?
options.npc_response: 'Two teams. Standard survey protocol. Neither reported back.' A pause. 'We have partial data suggesting rank C creature behavior in a registered rank F zone. We don't know why yet.'
options.memory_summary: Player asked about the missing survey teams on Floor 2.

options.label: Your incident reports are about Floor 2, aren't they.
options.npc_response: A fraction of a pause. 'You read people well.' She sets down the reports. 'Yes. Two teams. The irregularities are worse than the official summary suggests â€” I was deciding how much to disclose to new classifications.'
options.memory_summary: Player correctly deduced she was reviewing Floor 2 incident reports.

options.label: I completed the dungeon survey contract.
options.npc_response: 'Goblin patrol documented, crystal chamber located. This is clean work.' She marks the ledger and nods toward the door. 'Reward is being processed â€” check your System balance shortly.'
options.memory_summary: Player completed and submitted the dungeon survey contract.

options.label: I already submitted the dungeon survey.
options.npc_response: 'I know. It's on record. Good work.'

options.label: How do I officially join the Guild?
options.npc_response: 'Complete your first contract. Reach Rank E. Show you understand that the System's ranking exists to keep everyone alive, not to sort people into boxes.' She pauses. 'Some new classifications miss that distinction.'

options.label: That's all I needed. Thank you.
options.npc_response: 'Good luck out there.'

friendly_root.npc_text: Sylara looks up with something that isn't quite a smile but is warmer than her default expression. 'You again. What's on your mind?'
friendly_root.smart_observation: She's set the incident reports aside. You're not being treated as a new classification anymore.

options.label: The System's blind spots â€” how many are there?
options.npc_response: 'More than we're disclosing publicly. The Fracture didn't damage the System â€” it changed what the System chose to see. Some areas went dark deliberately, we think. Floor 2 may be one of them.'
options.memory_summary: Disclosed that System blind spots may be deliberate to trusted player.

options.label: Anything new I should know about?
options.npc_response: 'There's a contract board for that.' But she adds: 'The Riel twins came back from Floor 1 with something unusual â€” a marking on the wall they couldn't classify. I've asked them to file a proper report.'

options.label: Just checking in. I'll head out.
options.npc_response: 'Watch your flanks in the dungeon.'

dungeon_info.npc_text: 'Three registered floors. First floor â€” Rank F. Standard goblin patrol, slime colony in the east corridor, some oversized vermin near the crystal chamber. Good for calibrating your new abilities.' She pauses. 'Second floor has been irregular. Don't go there until you're stronger.'

options.label: Irregular how?
options.npc_response: 'Above your current pay grade. Stay on Floor 1.'
options.memory_summary: Gave dungeon briefing to new classification.

options.label: Understood. Thank you.
options.npc_response: 'Good luck.'

floor2_info.npc_text: 'Two survey teams. Standard protocol â€” three members each, proper gear, System compass active. Neither returned. We have signal data suggesting rank C behavior from registered rank F creatures. The System's classification data for that floor is unreliable.'
floor2_info.smart_observation: She's giving you the sanitized version. The actual data she's reviewed is worse.
floor2_info.perception_reveal: She knew at least one of the people who didn't come back. The way she doesn't name them is the kind of careful you do when names hurt.

options.label: I could look into it.
options.npc_response: 'Not yet. You're fresh from your classification. Come back when you've made Rank E and cleared Floor 1 properly. Then we'll talk.'

options.label: I've already been in the unmapped passage on Floor 1.
options.npc_response: A long pause. She reassesses you. 'You actually went in there. Without a compass bearing.' She looks at her records. 'Rank E. Come back at Rank E. I'll have a different conversation with you.'
options.memory_summary: Player revealed they explored the unmapped passage. Reassessment noted.

options.label: Understood. I'll stay on Floor 1 for now.
options.npc_response: 'That's the smart move.'

floor2_full_brief.npc_text: 'The first team didn't come back four weeks ago. The second â€” sent to find the first â€” didn't come back two weeks ago. What we got from the signal data: the creatures on Floor 2 aren't behaving like registered Rank F creatures. They're coordinating. Planning. The System has no explanation for why, because as of the Fracture, Floor 2 is partially outside System observation.' She meets your eyes. 'I'm telling you this because you're perceptive enough to find out anyway, and I'd rather you be informed when you do.'

options.label: Is this connected to the Fracture itself?
options.npc_response: 'Almost certainly. But I don't know how. Whatever the Fracture did to Floor 2 goes beyond what the System's current framework can measure. And that makes it more dangerous than anything I can rank.'
options.memory_summary: Gave full briefing on Floor 2 and Fracture connection to highly perceptive player.

options.label: I appreciate you being direct about it.
options.npc_response: 'Don't make me regret it. Stay on Floor 1 until your rank is actually suited for what's down there.'

survey_complete.npc_text: 'Your Guild record is updated. First contract marked complete.' She slides the ledger closed. 'You're formally on the Guild roster now. Future contracts will have better payout, and the equipment loan program is available to you.'

options.label: Good to know. Thank you.
options.npc_response: 'Keep filing clean reports. They make my job easier.'

guild_join_info.npc_text: 'Contract completion and Rank E is the formal threshold. Informally â€” show judgment. Not heroics. Judgment. Knowing when to fight, when to observe, when to come back with better information. We've lost too many people to heroics.'

options.label: Understood.
options.npc_response: 'Start with the board contracts.'

hostile.npc_text: Sylara's expression doesn't change but something in the room does. 'I'm going to ask you to leave Guild premises. Whatever you've done, this isn't the place to resolve it.'

options.label: Fine.
options.npc_response: 'Good day.'

name: The Gray Wanderer
description: A figure in gray who sits at the far edge of the market. No System profile. No Guild registration. No reaction to the passive classification scan.
flavor_text: The System does not acknowledge his existence. He seems comfortable with that.

root.npc_text: He doesn't react to your approach until you're standing directly in front of him. Then he looks up â€” not startled, just ready. 'You found something the System can't read. Or went somewhere it can't see. That's why you can see me.'
root.smart_observation: He speaks as if choosing from a list of possible phrasings â€” correct, but with the slight formality of someone who learned the language from text rather than conversation.
root.perception_reveal: He has no System shadow. No passive ping when you stand close. Not blocked â€” absent. Whatever the System uses to track and categorize, he exists outside it entirely.

options.label: Who are you?
options.npc_response: 'A question I've asked myself. I know what I was. I know what I'm looking for. Whether that constitutes a person or a purpose, I haven't resolved yet.'
options.memory_summary: Player introduced themselves. Asked who he is.

options.label: What is the void shard I found?
options.npc_response: 'A remnant. The Fracture didn't create the System â€” it gave the System permission. That shard is material from before permission was granted. It remembers what things felt like when the System wasn't watching.'
options.memory_summary: Player showed void shard and asked about its nature.

options.label: That passage in the dungeon â€” the System went silent.
options.npc_response: 'Yes. There are more of those. Places the System's observation doesn't reach. I'm mapping them. They have something in common, and I think it matters.' He tilts his head. 'You're the first person in Verath who's been in one.'
options.memory_summary: Player discussed the unmapped passage. He confirmed he's mapping System blind spots.

options.label: I need to think about this.
options.npc_response: 'I'll be here. Or near here. The System has trouble tracking me precisely.'

friendly_root.npc_text: He looks up before you're close enough that he should have heard you. 'I thought you'd come back. What did you find?'

options.label: I've been to Dungeon Floor 2.
options.npc_response: 'Then you've seen what I needed you to see. The creatures there â€” they're not acting on instinct. They're following something. A pattern that predates the System.' He leans forward slightly. 'Tell me everything.'
options.memory_summary: Player reported experience on Floor 2. Key intelligence gathered.

options.label: What's the next step in your mapping project?
options.npc_response: 'The dungeon. Specifically Floor 2. I can't go in â€” I'm highly visible to anything that operates outside the System's observation, which is exactly what seems to be down there. But you...' He considers. 'You might pass unnoticed. Especially carrying that shard.'

options.label: Just checking in.
options.npc_response: 'I know. Come back when you've been somewhere interesting.'

identity.npc_text: 'I came from somewhere the System doesn't cover. Whether that makes me an anomaly or a survivor depends on how you define both words. I'm looking for a way home, or a way to close the door behind me so nothing else comes through. I haven't decided which is better.'
identity.smart_observation: He's not being evasive. This is a genuine uncertainty â€” the kind you get from sitting with a question for too long without a framework to resolve it.
identity.perception_reveal: His hands, when he shifts â€” the proportions are slightly wrong. Not deformed. Just different. Like someone who learned to gesture from watching, not doing.

options.label: What door?
options.npc_response: 'The Fracture. It wasn't a natural event â€” it was an opening. The System came through something, and that something is still open. That's why the dungeons are irregular. That's why Floor 2 is outside the System's observation. The Fracture's edge is still active.' He pauses. 'I am, among other things, evidence of this.'
options.memory_summary: Disclosed Fracture theory to player with sufficient intelligence.

options.label: Where is home?
options.npc_response: 'Somewhere the System doesn't reach. I don't know if it exists anymore â€” the Fracture changed things on both sides. But the alternative to looking is deciding it doesn't matter. I'm not ready for that.'

void_explanation.npc_text: 'Before permission. Before the System decided it had the authority to categorize everything. The void shard is from that time â€” it doesn't resist the System so much as it predates the System's claim on it. Hold it near a System registration point and watch the ping fail. The System can't explain something that didn't ask for its classification.'

options.label: What was it like before the System?
options.npc_response: 'I don't fully know. I wasn't there, not in the way you mean. But the records suggest: more noise, less order. Harder to survive, easier to be something unexpected. The System improved life for most people. But it also decided what lives were possible.'
options.memory_summary: Discussed pre-System world with philosophically inclined player.

options.label: I think I'll keep it.
options.npc_response: 'I thought you would. It suits you. People who go into unmapped passages usually aren't looking for what the System has already catalogued.'

mapping_project.npc_text: 'Every place where the System's observation fails has something in common: they're near where the Fracture opened. The dungeon's unmapped passage is one. Floor 2, I believe, is another. If I can map them all, I can trace the Fracture's edge.' He pauses. 'That matters for reasons I'm still working out.'

options.label: I can help with the mapping.
options.npc_response: 'I was hoping you'd say that. You've already been to one site. The next one the System can't see is deeper â€” Floor 2 of the dungeon. I can't go in. But you can. Come back when you're ready for that, and bring the void shard. It helps.'
options.memory_summary: Player offered to help map System blind spots. Alliance established.

options.label: I'll think about it.
options.npc_response: 'Take your time. I'll be here.'

floor2_debrief.npc_text: 'The creature that looked at you like it was waiting â€” yes. They don't just exist in the dungeon. They're organized around something in the space below Floor 2. If the Fracture is a door, Floor 3 may be where the door is. The Guild has it sealed, which means they know something too.' He pauses. 'I think it's time to compare notes with someone in the Guild who might be willing to listen.'

options.label: The Guild Master might listen.
options.npc_response: 'Yes. She reads people well. Take what I've told you and see if she'll expand on what she knows. Between her operational data and my theoretical framework, we might be able to build a complete picture.'
options.memory_summary: Suggested bringing Guild Master into the investigation.

options.label: I'd rather work with you directly for now.
options.npc_response: 'Understood. We'll do it the slow way, then. Careful, though. When the System can't see you, it means nothing else can either â€” but it also means you have no backup if something goes wrong.'

name: Captain Aldis
description: The Guard Captain of Verath's market district â€” steady, watchful, carrying more political awareness than his rank usually calls for.
flavor_text: He got his rank six months after the Fracture. Whatever he did in those six months, nobody mentions it openly.

root.npc_text: The guard captain watches you approach with the particular stillness of someone who has assessed a lot of people at a lot of checkpoints. 'Move along.'
root.smart_observation: He's scanning exit routes, not threats. Like someone who expects to be followed rather than attacked.
root.perception_reveal: There's a second insignia under his collar â€” not the Guard's standard mark. A different faction symbol, partially visible when he turns.

options.label: What are the patrol routes in this district?

stat_gates.fail_message: He stares at you blankly. 'That's Guard business.'

options.npc_response: 'East gate at dawn and dusk. Market perimeter at noon. North residential at mid-afternoon. Why do you need to know?'
options.memory_summary: New classification asked about patrol routes.

options.label: How is the city holding up post-Fracture?
options.npc_response: 'Better than some. Worse than it should be. The classifications created stratification we didn't expect â€” Rank C citizens don't live near Rank F. The System sorted us and left us to figure out what that means.'
options.memory_summary: Discussed post-Fracture social stratification with new classification.

options.label: That's not a Guard insignia under your collar.

stat_gates.hint_text: Something about his collar doesn't quite match the standard Guard uniform...

options.npc_response: His expression doesn't change, which is its own answer. 'You have good eyes. Keep them to yourself.' A pause. 'And keep that to yourself as well.'
options.memory_summary: Player noticed the second faction insignia. Threat assessment: observant but controlled.

options.label: I have a record. I'm trying to do right by the city.
options.npc_response: 'You're either telling the truth or you're very good at lying.' A long pause. 'Stay clear of trouble for thirty days. Report any dungeon irregularities to me directly â€” not the Guild, not the board, me. Do that and we'll talk about the record.'
options.memory_summary: Offered probation deal to classification with criminal record. Awaiting results.

options.label: Carry on, Captain.
options.npc_response: 'Move along.'

friendly_root.npc_text: Aldis gives a brief nod â€” not warm, but genuine. 'Good day. Something I can do for you?'

options.label: Dungeon irregularities worth reporting.
options.npc_response: 'I'll pass that up the chain. Good. Keep doing that.' He marks something in a small ledger. 'For what it's worth â€” the record's less of a problem than it used to be.'
options.memory_summary: Player reported dungeon irregularities as agreed. Probation progressing well.

options.label: What faction is the second insignia for?
options.npc_response: A long pause. 'There are people who think the System's control of rankings and classifications has gone further than it should. Not against the System. Just... watching it. Making sure it stays in the lane it was supposed to stay in.' He tucks the collar. 'You didn't hear that from me.'
options.memory_summary: Disclosed faction membership to trusted, high-disposition contact.

options.label: Just passing. Good day.
options.npc_response: 'Stay clear of trouble.'

patrol_info.npc_text: 'Standard grid â€” east, north, market center on rotation. If you're doing dungeon work, the road's clear until midnight. After that it's a different situation.'
patrol_info.perception_reveal: The schedule he gave you is real but incomplete â€” there's a fourth route he didn't mention, and the timing is slightly off. Deliberate omission, not an error.

options.label: That's not the complete schedule.

stat_gates.hint_text: There's something off about that timing...

options.npc_response: 'Perceptive.' He looks at you more carefully. 'Standard protocol: never give a stranger the full picture. Move along.'
options.memory_summary: Player caught the Guard Captain withholding patrol information. High observational intelligence.

options.label: That's helpful. Thank you.
options.npc_response: 'Keep to the marked routes and you won't have trouble.'

city_talk.npc_text: 'Rank C citizens earn more Shards, live in better districts, get first access to Guild contracts. Rank F citizens work the dungeon's first floor and hope their classification improves. The System didn't say that's how it would be. But that's how it is.' He pauses. 'I'm not sure that was an accident.'
city_talk.smart_observation: He has political opinions well above a guard captain's usual scope. He's either unusually thoughtful or was something different before the Fracture.

options.label: The System created divisions it doesn't want to acknowledge.
options.npc_response: 'That's the polite version, yes.' A slight shift in his expression â€” not warmth, but recognition. 'Be careful saying that out loud around System registers. They track sentiment in cities now, officially for safety purposes.'
options.memory_summary: Player agreed with assessment of System-created stratification.

options.label: The rankings exist to keep people safe in the dungeon.
options.npc_response: 'Maybe. That was the original purpose. Whether it's still the purpose or just the justification...' He trails off. 'Above your pay grade. Good day.'

insignia_reaction.npc_text: 'Whatever you think you saw â€” you didn't. That's not a threat, just practical advice. There are things in Verath that run better when they're not observed. You seem like someone who understands that.'

options.label: Understood. My mistake.
options.npc_response: 'Good instincts.' He resumes his patrol route. 'Come back when you've made rank E. We might have more to discuss.'
options.memory_summary: Player handled insignia discovery with discretion. Promising contact.

deal_made.npc_text: 'Thirty days, irregularities reported to me. After that we'll revisit the record.' He resumes scanning the market. 'Don't make me regret the conversation.'

options.label: You won't.
options.npc_response: 'Good. Now move along â€” I have a market district to maintain.'

hostile.npc_text: Aldis doesn't reach for his weapon. He doesn't have to. 'I know what you've done. Walk away now, or we have a different kind of conversation.'

options.label: I'm going.
options.npc_response: 'Smart.'

options.label: I can be useful. Hear me out.
options.npc_response: A pause that could go several ways. 'Thirty seconds. Start talking.'
options.memory_summary: High-intelligence player attempted negotiation from hostile standing.

hostile_negotiate.npc_text: He's listening. Nothing in his posture suggests he'll decide in your favour, but he hasn't ended the conversation.

options.label: I know things about the dungeon irregularities that the Guild isn't sharing.
options.npc_response: 'Talk to me tomorrow. At the east gate, not here.' He doesn't confirm or deny anything. 'And keep this conversation off the record.'
options.memory_summary: Hostile-standing player leveraged dungeon intelligence to establish contact.

options.label: Never mind. I'll leave.
options.npc_response: 'Wiser choice.'

name: Vael
description: A tall researcher with ink-stained hands and the focused quiet of someone who has spent years reading things that most people don't know exist.
flavor_text: He was at his desk when the Fracture happened. He's been trying to understand it ever since.

root.npc_text: The scholar at the third-floor desk looks up from a spread of diagrams. His eyes flick to your System profile with the practiced efficiency of someone who evaluates classifications habitually. 'You're not one of the usual consultation requests.' He sets down his pen. 'What do you need?'
root.smart_observation: The diagrams on his desk aren't System architecture schematics like you'd expect. They look like pre-Fracture cartography.
root.perception_reveal: There's a void shard fragment in a sealed glass case behind him, labeled in a script you don't recognize. Whatever it says, he's kept it visible on purpose.

options.label: Can you tell me what actually caused the Fracture?
options.npc_response: 'The official record says: a destabilization event in the arcane substrate of the northern continent. My research says: something punctured through.' He picks up his pen again. 'Not in. Through. From somewhere else. The System came with it — or came because of it. We don't have consensus on which.'
options.memory_summary: New classification asked about the Fracture's origin.

options.label: What do you know about void crystals?
options.npc_response: 'Where did you hear about those?' He doesn't sound alarmed — more like someone calibrating how much to explain. 'Void crystals are material residue from pre-Fracture arcane resonance events. The System can't catalogue them because they predate its taxonomy. That makes them anomalous. Anomalous objects attract attention from the wrong people.'
options.memory_summary: Player asked about void crystals.

options.label: I have a void crystal. I was told you might be interested.
options.npc_response: He goes very still. 'May I?' He examines it without taking it, leaning forward. 'Floor one. That's unusual — void crystal formation at that depth suggests a fracture resonance point nearby. Somewhere the boundary between layers is thin.' He straightens. 'I'll pay five hundred silver for it, and I'll tell you what I find.'
options.memory_summary: Player brought a void crystal for examination.

options.label: Do you understand why the System assigns certain classes?

stat_gates.fail_message: He looks at you with polite patience. 'It's complex. Perhaps come back when you've had more time to develop.'

options.npc_response: 'The System reads potential pathways, not current capabilities. It's not measuring what you are — it's measuring what you're structurally suited to become. Divergent classifications happen when the potential map doesn't match any established template.' A pause. 'Those cases are rare and extremely interesting from a research perspective.'
options.memory_summary: Explained System classification mechanics to an INT-10+ player.

options.label: That's all I needed. Thank you.
options.npc_response: 'If you find anything anomalous — objects the System can't identify, areas where your compass reads incorrectly — I want to know about it.'

friendly_root.npc_text: Vael looks up without the initial evaluation. There's something almost like collegial warmth in his expression — the kind that forms between people who take the same things seriously. 'You again. Something new?'

options.label: I found something in the dungeon that didn't read correctly on my compass.
options.npc_response: 'Tell me everything.' He pulls out a fresh sheet of notes. 'Location, System response, any physical properties you noticed. This is exactly the kind of data I need.'
options.memory_summary: Player reported a compass anomaly in the unmapped dungeon passage.

options.label: I had a few more questions, actually.
options.npc_response: 'Go ahead.'

fracture_lore.npc_text: 'The Fracture happened in a single night. Pre-dawn in most of the continent. The northern monitoring stations recorded a 0.3-second event followed by a cascade — like a stone dropped into water, but the water was the fabric of how magic works.' He taps one of the diagrams. 'The System appeared in the first six hours. That's not a coincidence.'
fracture_lore.smart_observation: He's said this before — many times. The explanation is polished. But there's something underneath it he hasn't included.

options.label: You said something punctured through. Through to where?

stat_gates.fail_message: He hesitates. 'It's difficult to frame without more context. Ask again once you've seen more of the world.'

options.npc_response: A long pause. 'That's the question, isn't it. The instruments measured an inflow, not an explosion. Something came from outside the substrate boundary.' He meets your eyes. 'The System is not from Aethoria. I believe it arrived with whatever caused the Fracture. What it is — or who controls it — I don't know yet.'
options.memory_summary: Shared theory about the System's external origin with a perceptive player.

options.label: That's a lot to think about. Thank you.
options.npc_response: 'Most people don't ask. I appreciate that you did.'

void_lore.npc_text: 'The wrong people being: anyone who believes unregistered materials constitute a System violation. There are factions — some in the Guard, some outside it — who treat anomalous objects as threats rather than data.' He nods toward the sealed case behind him. 'I've had my research sanctioned once. The piece you see is all I kept.'

options.label: What do you think the crystals are?
options.npc_response: 'Pre-Fracture arcane nodes, partially crystallized. The material itself is inert — it doesn't do anything on its own. What it does is refuse System interaction. That's the part that makes people nervous.' He pauses. 'Also the part that makes it extremely useful if you need to act without the System knowing.'

options.label: I'll be careful.
options.npc_response: 'Please. And if you find more — bring them to me, not to the market.'

void_purchase.npc_text: 'Five hundred silver. I know that's less than the black market rate but it comes with a guarantee: I'll record the finding properly, I'll share any conclusions, and nobody outside this room knows where I got it.'

options.label: Deal. Take it.
options.npc_response: He takes the crystal with both hands and sets it in a padded case. 'Thank you. I'll have results within the week. Come back and ask for me by name.'
options.memory_summary: Purchased void crystal from player for 500s. Research ongoing.

options.label: Not yet. I want to know more about it first.
options.npc_response: 'Reasonable. The offer stands.' He hands back the crystal carefully. 'Don't show it to Guard checkpoints.'

class_lore.npc_text: 'There are forty-seven registered divergent classifications in the Conclave's records since the Fracture. The System assigned them regardless of what the individual expected or wanted. Several became significant figures.' He taps the edge of his notes. 'The common thread: they all made choices that didn't match any established pattern. The System noticed.'

options.label: Can the System see when someone is diverging?
options.npc_response: 'In real-time, probably. It's cataloguing behavioral data constantly. Whether it acts on that data before the divergence resolves is unclear. What's clear is: the final classification often surprises the individual. The System seems to wait until the pattern is complete.' He looks at you steadily. 'I mention this because your profile reads as... still in progress.'
options.memory_summary: Noted player's profile appears to be a divergent classification in progress.

options.label: Something to think about. Thank you.
options.npc_response: 'Come back if you want to discuss the implications.'

hostile.npc_text: Vael closes his notebook and looks at you with the cold clarity of someone who has made a formal decision. 'I don't think we should continue this conversation. I'll ask you to leave the floor.'

options.label: Fine.
options.npc_response: 'Thank you.'
